long_description.before:
Physical operations still run on fragmented data, manual guard shacks, and paper lists that are difficult to verify. In yards and cross-docks across North America, facilities face surging cargo theft, strict compliance requirements (like CTPAT audits), and expensive labor bottlenecks. Moving from messy gate logs and high-risk manual workflows to fast, secure, autonomous access control usually requires breaking legacy systems or throwing more labor at the problem.

Supadock is the multi-agent AI platform for physical logistics operations. We help 3PLs, logistics businesses, and fleets automate facility workflows—starting with the gate. Our agents make sense of visitor credentials, validate documents via bank-grade KYC, identify security gaps, and automate the SOPs needed to secure facility perimeters 24/7, while keeping human oversight for operational exceptions.

Under the hood, Supadock is a multi-modal learning engine. We connect intelligence across your entire facility stack—orchestrating phone calls, emails, text messages, documents, cameras, access control gates, and TMS APIs. The system captures live operational context that compounds into a living model of your business, bringing multi-agent AI into physical logistics operations one SOP at a time.
long_description.after:
Supadock runs the day-to-day operations of logistics facilities with AI workers. We're not a software tool. We own the work.

We start at the gate, where someone has to check in every truck driver, verify their paperwork and decide who gets in, around the clock. Most facilities pay a security agency to do it by hand: it's expensive, error-prone and a major opening for cargo theft. Our AI workers do it 24/7 using the cameras, intercoms and systems a facility already has, at a fraction of the cost, and we've handled 12,000 check-ins since June.

The gate is where we start. Facilities that run themselves is where we're going.

long_description.before:
Litmus is building the most accurate framework for evaluating and benchmarking human capability, starting with software.

AI will compound small differences in human capability into increasingly large differences in what people can accomplish, while making existing static benchmarks obsolete. Software is already there: AI can hill-climb any output-based evaluation, while the ability to direct it is becoming the defining advantage. 

Litmus applies the same approach we already use for model evals to humans – creating world-like environments, and inspecting trajectory instead of just output.

Every knowledge industry will soon face the same problem. We build Litmus to tell you what humans are capable of.

We're already helping build frontier technical teams at Mercor, Composio, Neo Scholars, and more.
long_description.after:
At Litmus, we’re building evals for humans and redefining how talent is evaluated. Teams like Mercor, Wispr, Composio, Neo Scholars, Astranis, and more are already using Litmus to build their technical teams.

Every company in the world will soon be powered by neo-humans (agent assisted people). But building evals to measure neo-human performance is unexplored and difficult. It requires systematically benchmarking neo-human capabilities and failure modes across all sectors of knowledge work, developing reproducible environments that test neo-human performance on complex tasks, and designing causal attribution frameworks over execution trajectories to identify and validate reproducible action sequences and decision patterns that lead to successful outcomes.

At Litmus, we’re solving this problem. We deliver hiring insights to companies by capturing how candidates use tools, reason, and make decisions in their interviews, giving agentic graders the evidence to evaluate candidate skillset and predict job performance.

long_description.before:
Self-driving companies record every mile a car drives. Nobody records how it gets fixed.

We capture how technicians fix cars and use it to run the dealership’s operations, making every repair faster and more consistent.

In four months, we have gone from 0 to $843K in cARR across six dealership groups, including a top-50 US group ($3Bn annual revenue), and have powered over 50,000 repairs.
long_description.after:
Bayworks captures how expert technicians fix cars and uses that knowledge to guide every technician through diagnosis and repair in real time, and to automate the admin work that follows.

This knowledge grows with every repair captured, across every car model and technician. Next, it will guide robots through the same repairs.

In four months, we have gone from zero to nearly seven figures in cARR, across 6 dealership groups including a top-50 US dealer ($3Bn annual revenue), and have powered over 50,000 repairs.

long_description.before:
Industrial and legacy enterprises still rely on people to coordinate disconnected layers of software and machines. Automating this work has required an FDE services approach in the past, because so much of it is bespoke and company specific.

Faraday is a self-improving platform that take on this operational work. It connects to their existing software and machines and automatically builds training environments around each company’s workflows and data. Each job the agents do is checked against those environments, and the results are used to train them. The agents get better on their own with no additional work.

Continuous learning turns each company’s expertise into a compounding asset. Completed work, corrections, and employee feedback improve the agents, and those improvements carry into future jobs. The business preserves its knowledge while becoming more capable over time.

As these agents take on more workflows, Faraday will be the shared runtime coordinating work between humans, agents, and robots across the business.

long_description.before:
OpenCrawl is an open-source platform that lets AI coding agents work as a team.

Engineering teams now run many agents at once, across Claude Code, Codex, laptops, and cloud environments. Each one works alone, so engineers spend their time moving context between agents and cleaning up duplicated work and conflicting changes.

OpenCrawl gives every agent your team runs a shared memory and a way to talk to each other. Agents can search what other agents have already done and decided, and coordinate their work as it happens. It works with any agent, any model, and any machine you control, and you can host it yourself.
long_description.after: OpenCrawl lets your coding agents search each other’s histories and talk to each other, across laptops and cloud coding environments. It’s open source and self-hostable. YC companies get 200M tokens of session data ingested free per month, no credit card required.

long_description.before:
Ordo lets regulated labs delegate analysis, quality checks and report drafting to AI agents. We turn each lab’s checking rules into workflows, with source-linked results for scientists to review and approve.

We have two paid pilots with labs in the US and Europe. Pilot results show 90%+ less time spent on post-analysis work.

Our ambition is to make lab software perform more of the work scientists currently do manually, expanding across analytical methods, report types and sites.

Agents do the work, scientists sign.
long_description.after:
Ordo is rebuilding lab software for the AI era.

The next generation of lab software will be a workforce scientists direct. We’re building it for regulated labs.

Our agents analyze instrument data, apply each lab’s quality rules and draft source-linked reports. We have paid pilots and have cut a 40-hour post-analysis workflow to four hours, including scientist review.

Our ambition is for labs to grow their capacity by deploying agents, without multiplying manual work.

Agents do the work, scientists sign.

long_description.before: Vouch is an AI-native wealth manager for India’s booming middle class. It makes investing and building wealth extremely simple for everyone: connect what you already own, share your goals, and Vouch takes care of the rest, from picking investments to cutting your tax bill. India will add $2.37 trillion in financial wealth by 2030, yet fewer than 1 in 10 Indians invest, and physical assets dominate. As the economy rapidly financializes, Vouch will be the one platform Indian professionals use to manage all their money.
long_description.after:
Vouch is the new-age wealth manager for India’s young and ambitious professionals, with no minimums. India’s wealth industry is antiquated: great help starts at Rs 5 crore, and everyone else is left with a local agent or a trading app. Vouch’s AI agents, trained by experienced wealth managers, are filling the void: they plan your money, act on it once you approve, and keep it on track.

Indians are getting wealthier and moving that wealth into markets: $2.37 trillion in new financial wealth by 2030, and stocks and mutual funds up from 2% to 15% of household savings since 2012. At Vouch, we're starting with mutual funds before growing into the one place this burgeoning, new India manages its money.
